renderer.note: Vendored directly rather than as a submodule. Only the Rust crates, the C++ scene engine and their build files remain here. 2026-09-16: crates/bridge routes `type: "web"` projects away from the scene engine — WallpaperEntry marks Web supported, ProjectModel parses `file`, ActivationInputs takes project models and splits build() (engine scenes) from build_web() (WebWallpaperDesc per assigned/mirrored display), active ids include configured web wallpapers, and the uniffi surface gains `web_wallpapers()` returning BridgeWebWallpaper for the Swift-hosted WKWebView windows. Local 2026-09-17 playback changes publish committed native pointer capability through a bounded renderer-instance relay, serialize consumer activation with the shared button tracker, gate the existing poller by consumers and pause policy, batch samples in one actor turn, and deduplicate only successful identical position/enter writes. Level-only native button reconciliation preserves held levels across video gating. These internal runtime changes do not alter the persisted or UniFFI schema. Local 2026-09-17 power work makes presentation suspension per display: BridgeActorState keeps suspended_displays beside the global presentation_suspended flag, ActivationInputs resolves each scene's and web descriptor's paused state from its own display (mirrors included), EngineFacade gains set_display_paused, a global resume re-applies the displays that are still hidden, and the new uniffi method set_display_presentation_suspended carries one display's decision without touching the others or the user's Play/Pause choice. System audio capture is gated on visible consumers — a scene that is presenting and has audio response enabled — so hiding every audio wallpaper stops the analysis while volume and mute stay independent controls; mouse polling follows whether any display still presents. Covered by crates/bridge/src/tests/display_presentation.rs.

sceneEngine.note: Property-script updates continue from the current dynamic value rather than restarting from the authored base each frame, preserving hover interpolation and explicit property writes. Script input serialization copies no live subscriptions. Synthetic regressions cover convergence, interrupted reversal and user-value replacement. Scene parsing, the scene runtime and the offscreen probes carry local fixes. Latest on 2026-09-16: property scripts bound to a layer's visible/origin/scale/angles settings are no longer dropped when the authored visible value is falsy; alignment anchors for image layers are owned by SceneRuntimeContext, and RegisterNode no longer re-seeds a registered anchor from the already-offset node translate, so a dynamic origin or scale can neither lose the anchor nor double-count it; offscreen_scene_probe requests the production device extensions and dumps node transforms. Also 2026-09-16: WPPuppetLayer copies share one playback state that SceneScript reaches as IAnimationLayer through SceneRuntimeContext::PuppetAnimationControl, with animationlayers visible/rate/blend bound to user properties; cursor hit tests run in layer-local space and consult a parse-time alpha coverage mask for cursor-scripted image layers; offscreen_scene_probe gains WE_TEST_CLICK_OFFSET. Also 2026-09-16: cursor input is mapped through the presented scaling viewport and global camera instead of the raw canvas, and named layers only receive cursor events inside the drawn content rectangle, so hit testing matches where cropped or letterboxed wallpapers actually draw; synthetic regressions cover the cropped-presentation hit test and letterbox rejection. Local 2026-09-17 playback changes repair shader/transfer/overwrite synchronization and propagate VkResult recording failures, share checked color-framebuffer caching, remove only proven redundant pre-clears, and add strictly bounded single-pass UNORM direct presentation while retaining the normal pipeline and all completion waits. Native scene commits publish pointer capability with transactional callback ownership and level-only button reconciliation. Compiled script export metadata preserves initialization, timers, live writeback and cursor semantics; generation-based material conversion and derived transform caches still repair destinations, and failed node registration restores masks/shared puppet state while releasing new subscriptions. Pose results now belong to the existing shared playback State, audio uniform packing reuses an owning buffer with fresh per-call snapshots, and particle mouse inverses are skipped only without current linked controlpoints. Also 2026-09-17: vector material constants resolve one curve per component and share the playback of the timeline named by `options.parent`, so a paused page-fold corner applies its authored first key instead of the static value, components without a curve keep their own value, and a missing or cyclic parent freezes that group on frame 0 after one logged error; offscreen_scene_probe's WE_TEST_DUMP_PASSES now dumps only the last sampled frame and appends each dumped pass's material slot constants to passes.txt, and tests/CMakeLists.txt links nlohmann_json into media_thumbnail_texture_smoke so that target builds. Follow-ups the same day: a material constant reaches its property script at the component count the shader declares (one as a float, two and four through the new ResolveVectorSetting, three unchanged), so a scripted vec2 corner is no longer handed over as text and returned as NaN; and authored timeline events are carried through ScalarAnimation::events, recorded by ScalarAnimationPlayback::Advance as the playhead crosses them (once per event for a stall longer than a loop, never on a seek) and drained each Tick — after the scripted values are re-evaluated, so a marker crossed by the first tick reaches an initialized handler — into the animationEvent export of the property and scene scripts bound to that layer, carrying the authored name and frame; the global engine.on list is run once per marker by the runtime, which also refreshes the engine object for it, rather than once per matching scene program. scene.getAnimation(name) is new: a null layer passed to __animationControl matches an authored name across every registered timeline. offscreen_scene_probe's dumped pass lines also record live visibility. Local 2026-09-17 power work adds src/Video/VideoDecodePump.{hpp,cpp}: a codec-agnostic, receive-first decode state machine (Reading/PacketHeld/Draining/Stopped/Failed) that resubmits a packet the decoder rejected with EAGAIN instead of releasing it, sends exactly one drain request per end of input and restarts the stream only after the decoder itself reports end of stream, polls cooperative cancellation between steps, bounds consecutive no-progress steps, and releases a held packet exactly once on seek, stop or failure. FfmpegVideoTextureSource drives it through a libavformat/libavcodec adapter, allocates its format context so an AVIOInterruptCB can abort a stalled read, publishes cancellation through an atomic flag, and distinguishes cancellation from failure so stopping records no error. src/Video/VideoColorConversion.{hpp,cpp} is the shared CPU/GPU colour contract: limited-range chroma uses its own 224 code-value excursion rather than sample-0.5, bit depth scales footroom and midpoint, and unspecified matrices are inferred by resolution and logged once instead of silently treated as BT.601. Platform/Apple/FfmpegVideoInterop.mm feeds both the CPU converter and the nv12_to_bgra kernel from that one parameter struct, and replaces the bare retained MTLTexture with an owned AppleVideoFrameLease that also retains the CVMetalTexture wrapper and the pixel buffer for as long as the frame can be sampled, with a single release function and an explicit hand-off of a poolable conversion destination; Vulkan/TextureCache holds that lease. New tests: tests/video_decode_pump_test.cpp (13 cases, including reproductions of the previous feed-first order losing a rejected packet and the reordered tail of every loop) and tests/video_color_conversion_test.cpp (9 cases of known pixels, colour bars and range/matrix separation); playback_gpu_test compares the Metal kernel against the CPU reference across both ranges and BT.601/709/2020. P02's first version adds content-rate pacing to the frame clock: FrameTimer takes a pushed FrameDemand whose content_period can only lengthen the tick interval, is ignored below the configured ideal frame time and is clamped to MAX_FRAME_DURATION, so the user's and the display's ceiling always wins and a bad period cannot stall a scene; Scene::single_video_source is set only by CreateVideoProjectScene, beside the construction that justifies it (one video texture, a copy shader, a NoOpShaderValueUpdater, no script, particle, audio or pointer input); VideoTextureSource reports frameDurationSeconds as the shortest plausible period over avg_frame_rate and r_frame_rate so a variable-frame-rate clip cannot lose the frames inside its tightest gap; TextureCache::ShortestVideoFramePeriod returns unknown when any live source cannot answer; and SceneWallpaper pushes the period from the render thread after each frame and on every stop/resume, reporting nothing for any other scene because an authored scene may change on a time uniform, a script write, a particle system, audio reactivity or a feedback texture that is not enumerated. Covered by five new cases in tests/timer/frame_timer_test.cpp, which scripts/check_renderer.py now runs.
